title: Precision Sputtering of Diamond and Boron Carbide with Plasma Focused Ion Beams for High-aspect-ratio Milling
content: The advancement in focused ion beam (FIB) technology has enabled precision manufacturing for a wide range of applications. In particular, the recent introduction of plasma ion sources has significantly expanded the range and length-scale of materials suitable for precision FIB processing. Both diamond and boron carbide possess a combination of properties that make them attractive ablator materials for inertial confinement fusion (ICF) targets [1-3]. Some of the target components call for precise fabrication of sub-micron scale features with very stringent dimensional and compositional requirements. Plasma focused ion beam (PFIB) technology could be well suited for such applications. Here, we present our findings on the fundamental sputtering characteristics of diamond and boron carbide films studied with a PFIB instrument and describe how they are applied for precision milling of high-aspect-ratio holes in these materials.
